journal.hardwrought.heat_that_holds.text: Clay lies in the beds of rivers and lakes. Laid in a burning fire pit, each lump bakes into a brick. Four bricks, put together in my hands, make a small brick furnace. It is slow and wasteful, but it gets metal hot, and nothing else I can make yet does.
journal.hardwrought.rust_in_the_rock.tex: In caves and cliffs there is stone flecked with rust-brown. That is iron. A stone pick breaks it out as raw iron; flint only scratches it. Tapping the rock with the pick while crouched tells me which way the ore runs.
journal.hardwrought.at_the_anvil.title: Something to strike on
journal.hardwrought.at_the_anvil.text: Raw iron from the furnace is still rock, only hot. The rock has to be beaten out of it. That takes three things, all made in my hands: a stump of three logs to strike on, a wooden mallet of boards, cord and a stick, and gloves of leather and cord, or the glowing metal burns my hand. Cows give the leather.
journal.hardwrought.the_first_bar.title: The first bar
journal.hardwrought.the_first_bar.text: Raw iron goes into the brick furnace until it glows. Then: the mallet in my main hand, the glowing lump in the other, and use the anvil. The lump is beaten until the bar's outline is filled. It has to stay hot; cold metal does not move, so back into the fire with it when it dulls.
journal.hardwrought.an_edge_of_iron.text: Three bars, heated and beaten together on the anvil, make an axe head; three more a pick head. A head and two sticks, put together in my hands, make the tool: an iron axe, an iron pick. The pick reaches the deeper metals, nickel, silver and the like. Quenched in water while it glows it gets harder. This is the first edge good enough to work a standing trunk.
journal.hardwrought.bench_from_the_trunk: A bench out of the trunk

I have no saw, but I have an iron axe and the forest has standing trees. I crouch against a trunk with the axe and keep working the same spot, stroke after stroke, far more than it feels like, until the trunk becomes a workbench where it stands. Now there is room for three by three.
journal.hardwrought.more_on_my_back.text: The woven pack sags as soon as it is full. Lashed to a frame of sticks with more cloth and cord, at the hewn bench, it would keep its shape and hold twice as much. After that, only leather will do.
journal.hardwrought.something_to_drink.t: Water straight from a river makes me sick sooner or later. Three boards at the hewn bench make a bowl. Dipped in water, then laid on a burning fire pit, the water in it boils clean. Let it cool before drinking, or it scalds.
journal.hardwrought.breaking_it_finer.te: Copper and tin only mix once they are ground to powder. At the hewn bench: a shaft from logs, a crank of boards and sticks on a shaft, and a crusher of boards, cobblestone, flint and a shaft. Set the crusher down, the shaft into it, the crank on the shaft, and turn it while ore lies in it.
journal.hardwrought.two_soft_metals.text: Copper is green-veined stone; tin comes from its own ore, or washed out of river gravel, a grain at a time. Both go through the crusher. Three parts copper powder to one of tin, mixed at the hewn bench, make bronze mixture, and the mixture melts into a bar of bronze in the fire pit or the furnace.
The hewn bench will not take metal work. A bronze bar, hot on the anvil, is drawn out into nails. With nails in my pack and a hammer in hand, I keep striking the hewn bench until it is nailed fast. The nailed bench makes everything a bench can make.
journal.hardwrought.tending_wounds.title: Tending wounds
journal.hardwrought.tending_wounds.text: A bite or a heavy blow leaves an open wound, and a wound left open can go bad. Cord or wool makes a bandage at the nailed bench. Against fever and a sick stomach: the white oxeye daisy, dried on the rack, and willow bark, which comes off birch when it is stripped with an axe. Each with a bowl of water makes an infusion that boils into tea on the fire.
journal.hardwrought.reading_the_rock.tex: Ore lies in long veins and bodies; a long straight tunnel at the right depth cuts more of them than any number of holes. Crouched with a pick against bare rock, I hear what lies behind it. A book and quill, worked at the nailed bench, becomes an atlas that keeps where I have been and what I found.
journal.hardwrought.clean_water.title: Better water
journal.hardwrought.clean_water.text: Boiling one bowl at a time is slow. Boards around sand, charcoal and gravel make a sand filter; charcoal, from logs in a furnace, goes into its bed and is used up. River or swamp water poured on top comes out underneath as fresh water, into a tank, a bucket or a bowl. Fresh is better, not safe: now and then it still makes me sick. Seawater it cannot clean at all; it stays in.
journal.hardwrought.pure_water.title: Water that is safe
journal.hardwrought.pure_water.text: Sand only takes the river out of the water. A candle of fired clay goes further: the sand filter set in terracotta around more charcoal makes a ceramic filter, and what comes through it is purified, wholly safe, faster than sand, and from anything but the sea. Draw it off with a bucket or a bowl, or let it run into a tank: poured onto the ground beside other water, it mixes and is spoilt again.
journal.hardwrought.fire_and_water.title: Fire and water
journal.hardwrought.fire_and_water.text: The brick furnace is slow and cannot do gentle heat. Bricks, coal and cobblestone make a forge: pieces are laid in its coals by hand and taken out by hand. A bellows of boards, leather and a shaft beside it, turned by a crank, makes it far hotter. Plunged into water while glowing, iron hardens; warmed gently afterwards, it loses its brittleness.
journal.hardwrought.a_stronger_arm.title: A stronger arm
journal.hardwrought.a_stronger_arm.text: The crank tires me long before the work is done. A water wheel of sticks, boards and a shaft, set across a flowing river with its lower paddles in the water, turns without tiring. So do the sails of a windmill of wool, sticks and a shaft, high up in open air. Everything after this wants a line that turns on its own.
journal.hardwrought.a_bath_of_metal.text: A forge brings metal to working heat and never melts it. Clay, sand and gravel make fireclay; fired in a furnace it becomes refractory brick. From those bricks: smeltery bricks for a floor and a ring of walls, a controller set in the wall, a drain with a faucet, and a casting table under it. Coal melts the soft metals; iron wants bellows on the wall, or coke.
journal.hardwrought.harder_than_iron.tex: Steel is made only in the smeltery. Iron and coal powder from the crusher melt together into steel once the bath is hotter than iron melts, about 1540 degrees: four parts iron to one of carbon. Pour it into an ingot cast, then forge a steel pick head. Steel breaks obsidian, which iron never will.
journal.hardwrought.marks_in_old_stone.t: Here and there old stones stand in a broken ring around a carved stone. Touching the carving, I understand its mark. A stick sharpened by rubbing it on stone, a stick and cord make a wooden wand. With it in hand, a right click opens a parchment to draw the marks on.
journal.hardwrought.a_ring_of_light.text: A circle drawn around a mark makes a shield of that element; an empty circle a plain one. It catches blows and arrows before they reach me. Wood barely carries the weight; the wooden wand and an iron bar make an iron wand that holds more. There is something deep below that only a shield will stop.
journal.hardwrought.a_golden_wand.title: A golden wand
journal.hardwrought.a_golden_wand.text: Gold carries the marks best of all. The iron wand, two gold bars and a shard of amethyst from the hollow geodes deep in the rock make a golden wand. It is steadier than any other, and I will need one at the very end.
journal.hardwrought.runes_on_the_blade.t: Lapis lazuli is worth nothing as a lump. Ground in the crusher, the powder is ink. With a piece in my main hand at the table of books, I lay runes onto it; more bookshelves around the table, rarer runes. Protection on armour will matter later.
journal.hardwrought.current_from_turning: A turning shaft only moves what it touches. Copper wire, iron and a shaft make a dynamo: set on the line, it gives two volts for every turn a minute. A copper coil set against it is where wire is strung from, and a lamp of glass and wire lights at the other end. Bare wire bites; hang it above head height.
journal.hardwrought.the_motor.title: A motor
journal.hardwrought.the_motor.text: Current turned back into turning: iron plates beaten on the anvil, copper wire, two coils of redstone wound round iron rods, and a shaft make an electric motor. Every electric machine wants one, and one lies on the altar at the very end.
journal.hardwrought.work_on_current.text: With a motor, current does the work: a press that flattens bars into plates, a crusher that grinds without a shaft, a furnace that heats without fuel, a saw that cuts more boards out of a log. Each is fed through a copper coil and wants about sixty volts.
journal.hardwrought.moving_it_along.text: A machine that has to be emptied by hand is half a machine. A pipe beaten from metal plates takes what comes out of it to the nearest chest or furnace with room. Bronze carries slowly, iron eight times as fast. A pipe wrench sets which side draws and which side fills.
journal.hardwrought.black_gold.title: Black gold
journal.hardwrought.black_gold.text: Layered rock that was once a sea floor sometimes smells of tar: crouched with a pick, I can sense a reservoir under it. Logs, iron, two shafts and an iron pick head make a drilling rig. Driven by a water wheel or a windmill, it bores down to the oil. Gas comes up first: give it a pipe out, or it waits for the first flame.
journal.hardwrought.the_column.title: The column
journal.hardwrought.the_column.text: Crude oil is good for nothing until it is parted. A refinery base, built around a copper still, stands over a fire; up to five trays of iron plates and pipes stand on it. Oil pumped into the base boils, and every tray catches its own cut: heavy oil, diesel, kerosene, naphtha, and gas at the top.
journal.hardwrought.the_heavy_cut.title: The heavy cut
journal.hardwrought.the_heavy_cut.text: The second tray from the bottom catches diesel. Drawn off with a bucket, or piped into a tank, it runs generators, and a bucket of it is one of the offerings at the very end. I should keep one aside.
journal.hardwrought.through_the_obsidian: Obsidian is too hard for iron; a steel pick gets through it. Water on lava only gives brittle cast obsidian; tempered in the smeltery at 1600 degrees, it becomes the real thing. A frame of it, lit with flint and steel, open a door to somewhere hot. The first passage is never stable: what I carry stays behind on this side.
journal.hardwrought.the_red_country.text: I came through with nothing, and the gate behind me is dead; I will wake here now if I die. The heat leaves me alone for a while, then it does not. Netherrack can be dug by hand, slowly. Gravel still gives flint, and the dark blackstone breaks into pieces like cobble.
journal.hardwrought.the_ash_grove.title: The ash grove
journal.hardwrought.the_ash_grove.text: Not far off there is always a grove of grey trees, cooler, where water stays. The ashcork's logs do not burn, and an axe strips thick bark off them that keeps the heat out; a full set of bark armour keeps three quarters of it off. The leaves give fibre and sticks, so the first tools can be made again.
journal.hardwrought.a_way_home.title: A way home
journal.hardwrought.a_way_home.text: Everything I left is waiting on the other side. Nether ores give iron again; metal thrown on a magma block heats on its own. With an iron axe I can hew a bench from ashcork. Blackstone pieces, quartz, gold nuggets and a magma block make a provisional stabilizer. Two set against the portal frame keep it open, and then what I carry comes along.
journal.hardwrought.a_steady_gate.title: A steady gate
journal.hardwrought.a_steady_gate.text: The provisional stabilizers only run in the heat of the Nether, or touching lava. The provisional one with quartz, gold bars and two blaze rods from the fortresses makes a real stabilizer that runs on current from forty-eight volts, anywhere. Two on each side and the gate stands for good.
journal.hardwrought.skulls_of_the_fortre: The dark fortresses of nether brick are guarded by tall black skeletons with bows and blades. Now and then one leaves its skull behind. I need three. Protection runes and a good shield help.
journal.hardwrought.souls_in_the_skull.t: An empty skull wakes nothing. Laid half a minute in blue soul fire, lit on soul sand or soul soil, it takes souls into itself and comes out shimmering. Three charged skulls on a T of four soul sand raise the Wither, far from home. When it dies, its souls gather into a nether star.
journal.hardwrought.the_seal.title: The seal
journal.hardwrought.the_seal.text: Under the deepest stone something is shut away. Chiseled deepslate, gold and four echo shards from the ancient cities of the deep dark make a seal stone. Down in the abyss, below y -180, it is set on the bedrock between four deepslate pillars, each with a soul lantern. The nether star set into it opens the way down.
journal.hardwrought.pale_light.title: Pale light
journal.hardwrought.pale_light.text: Below there is no north and no day. Pale crystals grow on the walls of the chasms. In the ruins stand old shafts of dim light; a pale shard rekindles one, and standing in its light carries me back up. I should never go further than my shards can bring me home from.
In the bare stone wastes of the Underworld ore lies open on the walls, and among it the hardest metal there is: adamantium. A steel pick breaks it out. It melts only in the hottest bath, coke and bellows. One bar of it lies on the altar at the end.
journal.hardwrought.finer_than_netherite: Four bars of mithril or adamantium around a cast blank of fireclay make an upgrade template. At the smithing table, a netherite piece traced with it becomes mithril, and mithril becomes adamant. The best gear I can have is what I want for the fights ahead.
journal.hardwrought.the_witch_king.title: The Witch King
journal.hardwrought.the_witch_king.text: The journals of the dead all point the same way: through the Graveyard and down through the bones of the Ossuary. Below them waits a king who was a witch. Armour holds little of his harm; I will need shields drawn with a wand, and runes. His mantle lets its wearer glide, and with a double jump, fly. In the ruins down there lie compasses whose needle turns to him.
journal.hardwrought.into_the_void.title: Into the void
journal.hardwrought.into_the_void.text: Blaze powder and an ender pearl make an eye that flies towards a stronghold. Twelve of them fill the frame there. Beyond is only void and a floor of light that holds me for thirty seconds. No block can be placed there while the dragon lives: without the mantle, I fall.
journal.hardwrought.the_dragon.title: The dragon
journal.hardwrought.the_dragon.text: The crystals on the lone pillars heal the dragon, each behind a ward that takes several hits, or a strong spell, to break. Break the wards, then the crystals, then the dragon. Rest on the broken fragments of the island. When it dies, it leaves its egg.
journal.hardwrought.raised_again.title: Raised again
journal.hardwrought.raised_again.text: The egg is not the end. Four end crystals, of glass, an eye and a ghast tear, set on the exit portal call the dragon back, stronger and angrier. What it leaves the second time is its heart, still warm.
Deep in the overworld lie geodes that are not amethyst: dark crystal humming with void. Its buds grow into clusters, and clusters break into shards. Four shards make a block of void crystal for the offerings; keep one more shard for the altar.
journal.hardwrought.a_temple.title: A temple
journal.hardwrought.a_temple.text: The heart wants a place made for it. The book's structures show three temples; the projection lays one out in the world, block by block. Gold, an eye of ender, crying obsidian, a void shard and blackstone bricks make the altar. It goes first, in the middle of the hall: it carries the roof.
journal.hardwrought.eight_offerings.text: Eight pedestals stand around the altar, each wanting one thing: a nether star, the dragon egg, a pale shard, a block of void crystal, an adamantium ingot, an electric motor, a bucket of diesel and a golden wand. Each shows its ghost until it is laid there.
journal.hardwrought.the_last_night.title: The last night
journal.hardwrought.the_last_night.text: When the temple stands and every pedestal holds its offering, the dragon's heart goes onto the altar. Then the night comes. I have walked from a flint in the gravel to here. One night more.

journal.hardwrought.arrival.1: We came down the shaft on the third day after the star burnt out. A darkness like nothing above. Our lanterns show twenty paces, then nothing. Brother Aldo says the seal was made by someone, long before us.
journal.hardwrought.arrival.2: There is no north. The compass spins like a dog after its tail, and the clock with it. I map by counting steps and by the drip of water. The rock is full of ore, open on the walls, glinting at the edge of the light.
journal.hardwrought.arrival.3: Odric found the pale crystals. They give a little light. Aldo says the old shafts that lead up drink their light and carry you home. I pray he is right, for I know no other way back.
journal.hardwrought.ore.1: Struck iron in the open wall, then copper, then something I have no name for. A man could get rich down here. If a man could get out again.
journal.hardwrought.ore.2: In the halls of dripstone the roof talks. A crack, a sigh, and a spear of stone comes down. It took Tamsin's leg. We do not go there without need, and never slowly.
journal.hardwrought.ore.3: The water is bad. All the water down here is bad, standing black in the low halls. Boil it, and even then. Three of us have the flux. The bread is going green.
journal.hardwrought.eyes.1: There are eyes in the dark. Two points, pale, at the edge of the lantern. While I look, they do not move. When I look away and back, they are somewhere else. Maren says it is the crystals catching light. Maren does not believe that.
journal.hardwrought.eyes.2: Last night they were closer. When Jory walked toward them, they closed, like a man shutting his eyes. There was nothing there. Only rock, and the cold.
journal.hardwrought.eyes.3: I hear steps behind me that are not mine. They stop when I stop. A beat late. When I turn, nothing. I have stopped turning round. Sometimes, when I sit still too long, something breathes.
journal.hardwrought.graves.1: Found a field of graves down here. Who buries their dead under the world? The soil is grey and soft, like ash that remembers being someone.
journal.hardwrought.graves.2: The dead get up here. Not all, not always. You hear the soil shift first. Steel works on them. Fire works better. Keep a light, keep moving.
journal.hardwrought.graves.3: Beyond the graves the bones begin. Walls of skulls, halls stacked with them to the roof. Aldo calls it the Ossuary. The air grows colder the deeper it leads, and it leads down.
journal.hardwrought.grove.1: We found a place to rest. Moss over everything, soft, and berries that glow on the roof like green lanterns. Nothing watches us here. No steps. We slept a whole night.
journal.hardwrought.grove.2: Odric thinks the eyes cannot come where the moss grows. I think they do not want to. There is a difference, and I do not like it.
journal.hardwrought.king.1: The whispers in the Ossuary say a name. Not a name: a title. A king who was a witch, or a witch who made himself a king. He sealed himself down here, or was sealed.
journal.hardwrought.king.2: His hall lies below the bones, they say. A citadel built out of the dark itself. Everything down here bends toward it: the passages, the water, the cold. Even the eyes, I think, are his.
journal.hardwrought.king.3: If anyone reads this: the way to him is through the graves, and down through the bones. Do not go. If you must go, go with light, and do not go alone.
journal.hardwrought.last.1: They are gone. Maren went to find an ascent shaft with three of the shards. Jory went down into the bones and did not come back. I cannot walk. My last torch is half burnt.
journal.hardwrought.last.2: Something breathes behind me when I sit still. So I do not sit still. I write so that I do not have to listen. A torch went out behind me today, and nobody was there.
journal.hardwrought.last.3: To whoever comes after: the pale shards light the old shafts. Stand in the light and it carries you up. Find the shafts. Do not wait as long as I did.

compendium.hardwrought.info.family.powde: Ore ground fine in a crusher. Powder needs no anvil: a furnace casts it straight into an ingot, and ground metals can be mixed into alloys.
compendium.hardwrought.info.family.rod: Drawn out on the anvil, four from one ingot. Rods go into coils, engines, circuits and machine parts; like any metal they melt back down as their metal.
compendium.hardwrought.info.family.plate: Beaten flat on the anvil from one ingot, or pressed cold in a plate press. Plates are what pipes, tanks and machines are built of.
compendium.hardwrought.info.family.ingot: An ingot is not crafted into tools. Bring it to working heat and forge it on an anvil into heads, blades, rods and plates.
compendium.hardwrought.info.family.raw: Raw ore does not smelt into a bar by itself. Heat it and beat the rock out of it on an anvil, or grind it to powder and cast that in a furnace.
compendium.hardwrought.info.family.raw_b: Nine pieces of raw ore packed together for carrying, and broken back down in the grid.
compendium.hardwrought.info.family.ore: Rich ground pays: inside an ore body every block drops extra, up to four more. Sneak and use a pickaxe on natural rock to read where the rich ground lies.
compendium.hardwrought.info.family.nethe: Ore in netherrack, for starting over in the Nether. It drops what the same ore drops in the overworld and wants the same pick.
compendium.hardwrought.info.family.tool_: A forged part. How well it was hammered, quenched and tempered is its quality, and it goes with the part into the tool. A rune written on the part works in fully.
compendium.hardwrought.info.family.armor: A forged armor part, put together with leather padding in the grid. Its craftsmanship decides the finished piece's protection and durability. A rune written on the part works in fully.
compendium.hardwrought.info.family.cast: A fired clay mould. On a casting table under a smeltery faucet it fills with the lowest metal in the tank. What comes out is rough and wants a grindstone.
compendium.hardwrought.info.family.unfir: A cast blank with a shape pressed into it. Fire it in a furnace before any metal is poured into it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.family.item_: Carries items, a batch at a time, to the nearest block that takes them. A pipe wrench sets each side to fill, draw or be cut off. Better metals move faster.
compendium.hardwrought.info.family.fluid: Carries liquids. Downhill from a tank they run by their own weight; uphill only a pump lifts them. The metal decides how much passes a second.
compendium.hardwrought.info.family.gas_l: Carries gas by pressure alone, from the fullest store to the emptiest. A store above what the weakest pipe holds bursts the line and lets methane out: bronze is for low pressure only.
compendium.hardwrought.info.family.mark: A faster mark, built on the one before: Mk II twice as fast, Mk III four times, Mk IV eight times on 240 V. Each draws more current. The Mk III crusher gives two powders an ore.
compendium.hardwrought.info.family.void_: Grows on budding void crystal, as amethyst does. Let it grow into a full cluster before breaking it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.family.steel: Steel holds an edge iron cannot and cuts like diamond. Plain steel rusts when wet: rust digs slower, hits softer and wears faster. A grindstone takes it off.
compendium.hardwrought.info.family.stain: Steel alloyed with chromium and nickel: tougher than steel, and it never rusts.
compendium.hardwrought.info.family.titan: Titanium is forged like iron and needs no alloying. Its armor weighs little more than half of iron's, and it never rusts. It does not harden when quenched.
compendium.hardwrought.info.family.tungs: The best a forge can make: the most durable and fastest forged tier, and its armor resists knockback. It never rusts. Netherite is worked up from it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.family.mithr: Worked up from netherite at a smithing table. Faster and keener than netherite, light as armor, and it takes runes more readily than anything but gold. It does not burn.
compendium.hardwrought.info.family.adama: Worked up from mithril: the most durable piece there is, the fastest tool and the heaviest blow. It does not burn.
compendium.hardwrought.info.family.ashco: Armor of ashcork bark. A full set keeps three quarters of the Nether air's heat off its wearer.
compendium.hardwrought.info.flint_shard: Broken out of gravel. With a stick and fibre it makes the first tools in the inventory square: nothing else is needed to start.
compendium.hardwrought.info.cobblestone_: Stone breaks into pieces rather than a clean block. Four make cobblestone again, and pieces make the first stone tools.
compendium.hardwrought.info.dirt_blob: Earth breaks into blobs. Four make a block of dirt, two a dirt slab. Dug by hand, fewer come out.
compendium.hardwrought.info.leaf_string: Dried leaf fibre, the first cord. It binds tools, makes bandages, and woven on a needle it becomes cloth for the first pack.
compendium.hardwrought.info.green_fibre: Stripped from leaves by hand. Green, it binds a tool as it is; hung on a drying rack in the sun it dries into leaf cord.
compendium.hardwrought.info.lighting_sti: Fire by friction. A campfire is set down laid, not lit: use the sticks on it to start it. They wear out after sixteen fires.
compendium.hardwrought.info.flint_hatche: The first tool, made from gravel and leaves alone. It cuts timber, slowly, and wears out fast: a beginning, not a tool to keep.
compendium.hardwrought.info.flint_pickax: Slower than wood and as fragile as gold, but it breaks stone, which bare hands cannot. Sneaking with any pickaxe on natural rock reads the ground.
compendium.hardwrought.info.stone_hatche: A better edge than flint, but too soft to hew a workbench out of a log: that wants an axe of iron or better.
compendium.hardwrought.info.stone_pickax: Breaks tin, zinc, lead, manganese, magnesium and aluminium ore. Nickel and the metals deeper down want iron.
compendium.minecraft.info.iron_axe: The first axe hard enough to hew a workbench: crouch, hold it against a standing log and keep working the same spot.
compendium.minecraft.info.iron_pickaxe: Reaches nickel, cobalt, chromium, titanium and the radioactive metals. Sneaking with it on natural rock finds rich ground within 160 blocks, with bearing and depth.
compendium.hardwrought.info.flint_dagger: The first real weapon: quick and cheap in stamina, but short in reach.
compendium.hardwrought.info.iron_dagger: Very fast and very cheap in stamina, with little reach.
compendium.hardwrought.info.iron_greatsw: Two-handed: high damage and reach, slow, and heavy enough to break a raised guard.
compendium.hardwrought.info.iron_halberd: The longest reach of any weapon, and it breaks guards, but it is weak against anyone inside 2.4 blocks.
compendium.hardwrought.info.filled_water: Eight drinks, 24 hydration each. Sneak and use it on water to refill. Held over a lit fire for five seconds it boils, which makes river and swamp water safe; seawater only gets saltier.
compendium.hardwrought.info.safety_lamp: Carried anywhere in the bag, it shows oxygen, carbon dioxide and methane in the panel (H) and warns of firedamp. A light that never sets firedamp off. Methane gathers at the roof: hold it up.
compendium.hardwrought.info.structural_a: Used on a built block, it lets the block hold on to a held neighbour without paying for the span: lintels, balconies, overhangs. One holds about five tonnes.
compendium.hardwrought.info.bronze_mixtu: Copper and tin, mixed but not yet bronze. A fire pit or a furnace casts it into a bronze ingot, with no anvil needed.
compendium.hardwrought.info.bronze_ingot: Harder than copper and a little short of iron: the first metal worth replacing a stone edge with, and the nails for the second workbench.
compendium.hardwrought.info.bronze_nails: Hammer in hand, nails in the bag: keep working a hewn workbench and it is nailed into the joined bench, which makes what the stump cannot.
compendium.hardwrought.info.smithing_glo: Hot metal burns a bare hand. Worn in the third square of the strap, under the lamp, they make it safe to hold.
compendium.hardwrought.info.wooden_hamme: A wooden mallet, the first smith's hammer: it moves one square of metal a blow.
compendium.hardwrought.info.hammer: Drives bronze nails into the hewn bench, and at the anvil moves two by two squares a blow. An iron hammer head and every armor part need at least this.
compendium.hardwrought.info.iron_hammer: Three by three squares a blow at the anvil. A steel hammer head needs at least this.
compendium.hardwrought.info.forge: A coal hearth that heats metal and keeps it hot. Its fire warms and cools slowly, which makes it the place to temper. Plain it reaches about 1300 °C, lined with refractory brick and blown by a bellows far more.
compendium.hardwrought.info.forge_hood: Hung one to three blocks over a forge, it catches the fumes of a 3×3 hearth. A gas pipe run off it lets them out, so the fire can burn indoors.
compendium.hardwrought.info.gas_pipe: A flue: run off a forge hood or set on a generator, it carries smoke and exhaust to its open end and out of the room.
compendium.hardwrought.info.bellows: Blows a forge or a smeltery hotter, but only while something turns it: a hand crank on it or a driven shaft.
compendium.hardwrought.info.fireclay: Clay with grit worked into it. Fired it becomes refractory brick, and four make a cast blank.
compendium.hardwrought.info.refractory_b: Brick that stands a forge's heat. Eight round a forge line it for more heat, and the smeltery is built of it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.wooden_anvil: A hardwood stump, end grain up. Hammer in the main hand, the hot piece in the off hand. Work on it reaches 85 %% craftsmanship at most, and it wears out after twelve pieces.
compendium.hardwrought.info.hewn_workben: The first bench, hewn out of a standing log with an axe of iron or better. It makes only the early things: boards, handles, a chest, the first metal tools and the bench that replaces it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.nailed_workb: The joined bench, nailed together from a hewn one where it stands. It makes everything a crafting grid can.
compendium.hardwrought.info.brick_furnac: The first furnace, from four bricks in the inventory square. Half as fast as stone and wasteful with fuel: it exists to be replaced.
compendium.hardwrought.info.drying_rack: Dries what hangs on it — green fibre into cord, oxeye daisy into chamomile — but only in daylight, under open sky and without rain. In the Nether six times as fast.
compendium.hardwrought.info.starter_back: Without a pack the main inventory is closed. The woven pack opens it and carries 85 kg. A worn pack is never lost on death.
compendium.hardwrought.info.frame_backpa: The woven pack lashed to a frame of sticks: it carries 95 kg.
compendium.hardwrought.info.basic_backpa: Opens a second page of nine slots behind the main grid and carries 110 kg. The pack's page has its own button under every container.
compendium.hardwrought.info.pointed_stic: A stick rubbed to a point on stone: the start of a sewing needle.
compendium.hardwrought.info.sewing_needl: Held in the main hand with leaf cord in the other, used for a while, it weaves cloth. With cloth in the other hand it sews the woven pack.
compendium.hardwrought.info.iron_sewing_: Forged at the anvil. It weaves in three seconds what a wooden needle takes ten for, and lasts far longer.
compendium.hardwrought.info.woven: Cloth woven from leaf cord on a needle. Sewn on the needle, four make the woven pack.
compendium.hardwrought.info.compendium: This book. R over anything shows how it is made, U what it is used in. A thing never held is a shadow; holding one for a few seconds, or working with it, studies it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.atlas: Draws the land around you while it is in the bag, and keeps it. M opens it. A right click marks a place with a name and a symbol, where you died is marked with a skull, and other bearers near you are drawn in it too.
compendium.hardwrought.info.shaft: Carries turning along its axis. A line has one speed: every part turns at a fixed ratio of the others. Crouch with an empty hand on a turning part to read its speed and load.
compendium.hardwrought.info.crank_box: Creative only: turns a line at 32 RPM with all the strength it could want.
compendium.hardwrought.info.hand_crank: Turns a line at 16 RPM while you crank it, with a strength of 160: enough for one starter crusher, not two.
compendium.hardwrought.info.tree_creakin: A creaking heart grown in an ordinary tree, in its bark. Between logs of its own wood it wakes at night and calls a creaking of the same wood.
compendium.hardwrought.info.burnt_torch: A torch that burnt down after a day. Flint and steel, a fire charge or a burning torch lights it again where it hangs.
compendium.hardwrought.info.burnt_lanter: A lantern that burnt down after three days. Flint and steel, a fire charge or a burning torch lights it again.
compendium.hardwrought.info.starter_crus: Stone jaws that grind raw ore into powder while something turns them: a hand crank or a driven shaft. Ore goes in by using it, powder comes out with an empty hand.
compendium.hardwrought.info.coal_powder: Ground coal. In the smeltery it dissolves into molten iron as carbon: four parts iron to one of carbon make steel.
compendium.hardwrought.info.lapis_lazuli: The ink of enchanting: runes are written onto a piece with it at an enchanting table, one measure for every six squares of rune.
compendium.hardwrought.info.mithril_powd: An ink for runes. A rune written in it reaches one level past the enchantment's highest, and a piece carrying one holds an extra rune.
compendium.hardwrought.info.adamantium_p: The finest ink for runes. A rune written in it reaches two levels past the highest, and a piece carrying one holds three more runes.
compendium.hardwrought.info.cogwheel: Teeth on a shaft: a cogwheel beside it on a parallel axle turns the other way at the same speed.
compendium.hardwrought.info.large_cogwhe: A small cogwheel across its corner turns twice as fast. Gearing a machine up makes it faster and heavier to drive at once.
compendium.hardwrought.info.gearbox: Takes a line round a corner: an axle on every face, opposite faces turning opposite ways.
compendium.hardwrought.info.water_wheel: Turns with a river's current or falling water, up to 32 RPM. Set it across the river with its lower paddles in the water; still water turns nothing.
compendium.hardwrought.info.windmill: Turns with the wind, 4 to 24 RPM, up to 1024 strength. The higher, the windier; rain and storms help. Most of its five-block circle has to be open air.
compendium.hardwrought.info.belt: Used on a shaft and then on a parallel one up to eight blocks away: the two turn together.
compendium.hardwrought.info.ritual_altar: The heart of the temple. Set it first: every block the plan has in place round it stands as if on the ground. With every offering laid, the dragon's heart on it begins the ritual. Asked early, it marks what is still wrong.
compendium.hardwrought.info.ritual_pedes: Eight stand round the ritual altar, each wanting one offering by its place, shown as a pale ghost until it is laid there.
compendium.hardwrought.info.budding_void: Grows void crystal on its faces, as budding amethyst does. It cannot be picked up: broken, it is gone.
compendium.hardwrought.info.void_crystal: From void crystal geodes deep in the overworld. A block of void crystal is one of the ritual's offerings.
compendium.hardwrought.info.steel_ingot: Made only in the smeltery: iron and coal powder melted together. It forges like iron, only harder. Plain steel rusts when wet.
compendium.hardwrought.info.stainless_st: Steel, chromium and nickel alloyed in the smeltery at 1550 °C. It never rusts.
compendium.hardwrought.info.tungsten_ste: Steel and tungsten, which alloy only at 3422 °C: a smeltery on coke with a bellows.
compendium.hardwrought.info.titanium_ing: Too hard for any furnace: bring it to working heat in a forge, or melt it in the smeltery. It needs no alloying.
compendium.hardwrought.info.smeltery_bri: A smeltery's floor lies under its whole tank, and a ring of bricks, glass, drains and one controller stands round it on every layer.
compendium.hardwrought.info.smeltery_gla: A window in the smeltery wall, to see the metal standing in the tank.
compendium.hardwrought.info.smeltery_dra: Where metal leaves the smeltery: a faucet on its outside pours into a casting table below.
compendium.hardwrought.info.smeltery_con: Set into the wall facing out, it finds the tank behind it and burns the fuel: coal 1250 °C, 1650 °C with a bellows; coke 2000 °C, far more with one. Click a layer in its screen to pour that metal next.
compendium.hardwrought.info.faucet: On a smeltery drain, it pours the lowest metal in the tank into the cast below. A redstone signal makes it pour again as soon as the cast is empty.
compendium.hardwrought.info.casting_tabl: Holds a cast under a faucet. A cast blank laid on it takes the shape of a bar or part pressed into it. A hopper underneath takes out what has set.
compendium.hardwrought.info.coke: Coal baked in a furnace. It burns twice as long as coal and much hotter: a smeltery melts iron on it, and tungsten on coke with a bellows.
compendium.hardwrought.info.smeltery_tan: A wall block holding four buckets of lava. The smeltery burns it when its fuel slot is empty, a bucket lasting five minutes.
compendium.hardwrought.info.cast_blank: Laid on a casting table, it takes the shape of a bar or part pressed into it. Four bars of mithril or adamantium round one make an upgrade template.
compendium.hardwrought.info.rune_stone: Found in rings of old stone in the overworld. Right-click the carving to learn its rune for good.
compendium.hardwrought.info.wooden_wand: Right-click opens the parchment to draw runes on; hold G to draw on the move. It carries spells up to tier 2. An overloaded wand wears fast and may break.
compendium.hardwrought.info.iron_wand: Carries spells up to tier 4 and steadies them a little.
compendium.hardwrought.info.golden_wand: Carries spells up to tier 5 and steadies them the most, but wears out sooner than iron.
compendium.hardwrought.info.mithril_wand: Carries spells up to tier 6, steadier than gold, and lasts.
compendium.hardwrought.info.void_crystal: Carries spells up to tier 8, the steadiest of all, and overload costs it only half the stability it costs other wands.
compendium.hardwrought.info.void_ink: Void crystal ground with an ink sac. Enchanting: a rune one level over its highest, two runes more on the piece. Scrolls bound in it hold steadier.
compendium.hardwrought.info.parchment: Three sheets of paper and leather. With ink, a drawing at the Mage Table is bound to it as a scroll.
compendium.hardwrought.info.rune_ink: What a scroll is written in. Void ink binds steadier.
compendium.hardwrought.info.scroll: A spell bound with care at a Mage Table. Use it: it is cast at once, without a wand, as well as it was drawn. Then it is gone.
compendium.hardwrought.info.mithril_upgr: Works a netherite piece up to mithril. Hold the piece, carry the template and a bar, use a smithing table and trace the figure of eight: the trace decides its craftsmanship.
compendium.hardwrought.info.adamant_upgr: Works a mithril piece up to adamant. Hold the piece, carry the template and a bar, use a smithing table and trace the spiral: the trace decides its craftsmanship.
compendium.hardwrought.info.dynamo: Turns the driveline into current: 2 V per RPM, and heavier to turn the more current is drawn. Wire it through a copper coil. Asked too much, it lets go for five seconds.
compendium.hardwrought.info.electric_dri: The dynamo the other way round: current in through a copper coil, turns out along its axle. 1 RPM per 2 V, and strength for up to 4 A; it draws what the line asks of it. Held still it draws five times its rating and trips a breaker. Its brushes wear while it turns; two graphite brushes renew them below a quarter.
compendium.hardwrought.info.insulator: What a line is strung from. Bare wire bites from 30 V, so a line belongs above head height. Above 150 V it flashes over in the rain.
compendium.hardwrought.info.electric_lam: Light with no fuel, as bright as its voltage: full at 60 V, dark below 12. Above 75 V the filament burns out; a coil of thin wire rewinds it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.copper_wire: Thin wire: 0.04 Ω a block, 4 A, 16 blocks a span. Over its rating it glows and burns through. Bare wire bites whatever touches it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.copper_cable: Four wires' worth: a quarter of the loss, 16 A, 24 blocks a span. Heavy loads like the arc furnace need it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.voltmeter: Held to any point: voltage, current, how hard the wires are worked and what the network gives and loses. Read it before you touch anything.
compendium.hardwrought.info.mast: A timber pole four blocks tall, set up in one piece. Its wire hangs above a standing player's head, and the pole bites nobody.
compendium.hardwrought.info.battery: Charges while the line stands above its 54 to 62 V and gives back below. A hand crank's 32 V never fills it. More than 8 A in or out boils the acid.
compendium.hardwrought.info.basic_crushe: Ore into powder on current, 1.5 A at 60 V. Standing idle it takes nothing. An electric furnace behind it with a hopper between smelts what it grinds.
compendium.hardwrought.info.electric_fur: Smelts what a furnace smelts, with no fuel: 2 A at 60 V.
compendium.hardwrought.info.sawmill: Half as many boards again out of a log as a hand gets, and it cuts raw silicon into wafers.
compendium.hardwrought.info.plate_press: An ingot in, a plate out, with no hammer and no heat. It also presses plastic sheet and electrical steel.
compendium.hardwrought.info.lathe: Turns a steel rod into a fine gear, the part a sorting mechanism counts with. Runs on current.
compendium.hardwrought.info.tube_mill: Rolls a bronze plate into a tube section, what storage tubes are made of. Runs on current.
compendium.hardwrought.info.storage_tube: Leads from the storage ports back to the storage desk. Nothing is kept in it: the desk reaches along it into the chests.
compendium.hardwrought.info.storage_port: Set against a chest, it sorts into it and fetches out of it. Against a furnace's side it feeds it, underneath it empties it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.storage_desk: Where the store room is worked from: every chest with a port on the tubes, taken from and put away into as one. Everything stays in its chest. It wants current: through a copper coil on the desk itself, or on any tube or port of the store room.
compendium.hardwrought.info.fine_gear: Turned on the lathe from a steel rod: small and true enough to count with.
compendium.hardwrought.info.tube_section: A bronze plate rolled round and seamed in the tube mill: what storage tubes are made of.
compendium.hardwrought.info.sorting_mech: The works of a storage port: what tells one thing from another and sends it the right way.
compendium.hardwrought.info.copper_coil: How a line joins a dynamo, a battery or a machine: set it against any face and string the wire to it. Several coils carry a line on through a machine.
compendium.hardwrought.info.gas_tank: Holds 256 units of gas at 20 bar. An empty canister held to it takes 16 units; a full one empties back into it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.refinery_bas: Stands over a fire and boils crude oil, 100 mB a second, keeping the bitumen at its foot. Up to five trays on top catch the other cuts; what has no tray is flared off.
compendium.hardwrought.info.refinery_sta: A tray catches the cut that matches its height: heavy oil, diesel, kerosene, naphtha, then LPG at the fifth.
compendium.hardwrought.info.cracker: Over a fire, it cracks heavy oil into diesel and gasoline, with some LPG.
compendium.hardwrought.info.reformer: Over a fire, it turns naphtha into gasoline, with a little LPG.
compendium.hardwrought.info.lpg_canister: Burns in a gas burner or a furnace. Refilled at a gas tank.
compendium.hardwrought.info.bitumen: The heaviest cut, left at the foot of the column. It burns, and feeds later chemistry.
compendium.hardwrought.info.heavy_oil: The cracker turns it into diesel and gasoline. It burns long in a furnace.
compendium.hardwrought.info.diesel: What the diesel generator runs on best.
compendium.hardwrought.info.kerosene: Burns in the petroleum lamp, ten days to a bucket, and runs a diesel generator at 90 %%.
compendium.hardwrought.info.naphtha: Feedstock: the chemical reactor makes plastic, silicone and medicine of it, and the reformer gasoline.
compendium.hardwrought.info.gasoline: Runs the gasoline engine: a bucket lasts about eight minutes.
compendium.hardwrought.info.light_fracti: Light spirit from the still. It runs a gasoline engine at 70 %%. A bottle is a third of a bucket and pours into a tank.
compendium.hardwrought.info.fuel_fractio: Fuel from the still. It burns in a furnace, giving its bottle back, and runs a diesel generator at 75 %%.
compendium.hardwrought.info.crude_oil: From oil lakes or a drilling rig. A still over a fire, or a refinery column, parts it into its cuts. It floats on water, drags at whatever wades in, and burns.
compendium.hardwrought.info.gas_canister: Held to a drilling rig or a gas tank, it draws 16 units of gas.
compendium.hardwrought.info.natural_gas_: Furnace fuel, giving the canister back. Held to a gas burner it lasts ten minutes; a gas tank takes it back.
compendium.hardwrought.info.raw_sulfur: Comes out of crude oil in the still, impure. Run through the still again it becomes nearly pure sulfur.
compendium.hardwrought.info.sulfur: Turns resin into rubber in the chemical reactor.
compendium.hardwrought.info.salt: From seawater, dried in a salt pan or the still. The electrolyser makes caustic soda and chlorine of it, and it goes into an electrolyte drink.
compendium.hardwrought.info.still: A copper pot still, working only with fire directly under it. It parts crude oil into four products, dries seawater to salt, refines sulfur and distils mash into spirit.
compendium.hardwrought.info.drilling_rig: Bores through the rock under it until it strikes oil or gas, then pumps. A hand crank is too weak for it. Gas with no pipe on top escapes as methane, and explodes at the first flame.
compendium.hardwrought.info.mechanical_p: Turned by a shaft, it drives a fluid run: the only thing that lifts a liquid uphill. Set in water it draws the water itself; a lake or the sea never runs dry.
compendium.hardwrought.info.electric_pum: Pushes four times what a mechanical pump does, on current through a coil.
compendium.hardwrought.info.fluid_tank: Holds 16 buckets of one liquid, shown behind its glass. An empty hand reads it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.pipe_wrench: Used on a side of a pipe. Towards a block it goes filling, drawing, cut off; towards another pipe joined and cut off.
compendium.hardwrought.info.burning_stac: Burns what nobody wants: gas a line brings it, firedamp in the air beside it — safely — and whatever burns in the tank under it. It gives off a lot of carbon dioxide, which sinks round it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.redstone_coi: Goes into motors, heating elements and fuel injectors.
compendium.hardwrought.info.electric_mot: Turns the crushers, sawmills, presses and pumps, and in a housing of its own on the driveline it is an electric drive. Built from a stator, a rotor, a commutator, two graphite brushes, two bearings and a housing. One is also an offering of the ritual.
compendium.hardwrought.info.stator: The motor's field: wound poles in an iron ring.
compendium.hardwrought.info.rotor: The part of a motor that turns: a wound drum on its shaft.
compendium.hardwrought.info.commutator: Turned from a copper rod on the lathe. Carries the current onto the turning rotor.
compendium.hardwrought.info.graphite_bru: Turned from a graphite electrode on the lathe, eight at a time. They wear in an electric drive and are changed in pairs.
compendium.hardwrought.info.motor_housin: The shell a motor is built into.
compendium.hardwrought.info.motor_contro: Fitted to an electric drive: starts it gently, holds it to its rating when held still, and an empty hand sets its speed in quarters of the voltage.
compendium.hardwrought.info.wire_drawer: A machine on current: a tungsten rod into four filaments, a nichrome rod into four lengths of nichrome wire, a copper rod into three of copper wire.
compendium.hardwrought.info.glass_kiln: A machine on current: glass blown into four bulbs, a pane drawn into two tubes.
compendium.hardwrought.info.autoclave: A machine on current: a bandage steamed into a sterile dressing.
compendium.hardwrought.info.electric_lig: A tungsten bulb in a shade, wired directly. Full light on 60 V for 25 W. The bulb burns out after four hours of light; a new light bulb mends it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.arc_floodlig: An arc lamp for the 240-volt line, 960 W. While it burns no monster spawns within 32 blocks, not even in the autumn fog, and monsters within 24 keep out of its light unless close on their prey. Its electrodes last two hours of light.
compendium.hardwrought.info.motion_lamp: Dark until something moves within 8 blocks; then lit for ten seconds and giving a redstone signal, enough to ring an alarm bell.
compendium.hardwrought.info.alarm_bell: Rings while it has a redstone signal and current: wakes everyone asleep within 32 blocks, and draws every idle monster that hears it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.electric_hea: Warms the room it stands in to its thermostat, 120 W. Spread over the room: one room well, a hall poorly. Open doors let the heat out. An empty hand sets the thermostat.
compendium.hardwrought.info.air_cooler: Cools the room it stands in to its thermostat: draws 180 W and pumps out two and a half times that. An empty hand sets the thermostat.
compendium.hardwrought.info.ventilation_: Set in a wall facing into the room: draws gas out of the room and blows it out behind, eight units a second.
compendium.hardwrought.info.refrigerator: Food in it goes off at a quarter of the speed while it has current.
compendium.hardwrought.info.freezer: Food in it does not go off at all while it has current.
compendium.hardwrought.info.heat_lamp: Warms whoever is near it like a working fire, and thaws frostbite.
compendium.hardwrought.info.bedside_moni: A bed within two blocks of it is a sickbed: asleep in it you heal half a heart a second and recover from illness two and a half times as well. In Ultra it heals only a dressed wound.
compendium.hardwrought.info.ice_box: Food in it goes off at half the speed while there is ice in it. A block of ice lasts half a day, packed ice four times as long, blue ice sixteen.
compendium.hardwrought.info.charging_sta: Charges up to five cells, or devices and lined chestplates with their cells in them, from the line: up to 240 W shared out, each cell no faster than it takes a charge, four fifths of it kept.
compendium.hardwrought.info.assembly_ben: The rung above the nailed bench: carried devices and cells are laid out on it part by part, and nothing lower makes them. It keeps what lies on it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.conveyor: A belt over rollers, turned through the axle across it by a shaft or an electric drive. One length drives the next. Carries what lies on it along, and at the end puts it into whatever holds things in front of it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.assembler: Makes what the drawing in it shows from the parts put into it, eight seconds a piece at full power. Joined to a storage network by its tubes, the desk orders from it what the store room has none of, and it fetches the parts it lacks from the network.
compendium.hardwrought.info.tesla_tower: The foot of a Tesla tower, fed at 960 V (two transformers up from a 60 V line), 900 W. Built whole — three resonant coils on it, the top load on them, a capacitor bank against it — it charges every cell carried within 24 blocks, lights electric lights in reach without wire, and strikes monsters within 16 blocks with arcs. Metal armour near the top load draws arcs too, and in a thunderstorm it calls the lightning.
compendium.hardwrought.info.resonant_coi: Three stand on a Tesla tower's foot.
compendium.hardwrought.info.top_load: Goes on a Tesla tower's three coils: where the arcs leave from.
compendium.hardwrought.info.capacitor_ba: Stands against a Tesla tower's foot: holds what the tower spends, 20 kJ.
compendium.hardwrought.info.spark_gap: Fires a Tesla tower's coil. The part of its foot that wears.
compendium.hardwrought.info.drawing: Use a blank drawing on an assembly bench with work laid out on it: it is drawn, if you have studied what it makes. Put it into an assembler.
compendium.hardwrought.info.machine_oil: Use it on an electric machine: its bearings are oiled for two hours of work. Dry, a machine wears six times as fast.
compendium.hardwrought.info.service_kit: New bearings and gaskets for a worn or seized machine.
compendium.hardwrought.info.coil_winder_: Winds twice as fast as the first mark.
compendium.hardwrought.info.wire_drawer_: Draws twice as fast as the first mark.
compendium.hardwrought.info.glass_kiln_m: Blows twice as fast as the first mark.
compendium.hardwrought.info.lead_acid_pa: 10 Wh, takes a charge at 60 W, weighs 2.5 kg. Cheap and heavy.
compendium.hardwrought.info.nickel_iron_: 20 Wh, takes a charge at only 20 W, weighs 2 kg. Never wears.
compendium.hardwrought.info.silver_zinc_: 40 Wh, takes a charge at 150 W, weighs 0.6 kg. Worn out after three hundred full charges.
compendium.hardwrought.info.headlamp: Worn on the head: a carried light that does not burn out, 5 W. Sneak and use it to switch it off or on.
compendium.hardwrought.info.night_vision: Worn on the head: see in true darkness at once, 8 W. Bright light blinds through them.
compendium.hardwrought.info.exoskeleton: Worn on the legs: carry three times as much before the weight tells, a wound slows you half as much, and you break blocks a little faster. 15 W standing, 35 W walking. Flat, it is a heavy frame that makes you carry less.
compendium.hardwrought.info.electric_dri: Digs stone and earth faster than any hand tool of its bit's metal, 120 Ws a block. Click a drill bit onto it; with no bit or no charge it is a block of metal.
compendium.hardwrought.info.chainsaw: Cuts wood fast, and a log cut at the foot of a tree brings the whole tree down. Sneak to cut one log. Click a saw chain onto it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.ore_scanner: Use it: a pulse that makes every ore within 12 blocks glow for you, and says what it found. 600 Ws a pulse.
compendium.hardwrought.info.heated_linin: Click it onto a chestplate: worn, it warms you toward comfort when it is cold, up to 15 °C, 3 W a degree. Charge it with the chestplate in a charging station.
compendium.hardwrought.info.cooled_linin: Click it onto a chestplate: worn, it cools you toward comfort when it is hot, up to 15 °C, 3 W a degree. Charge it with the chestplate in a charging station.
compendium.hardwrought.info.steel_drill_: 600 blocks in an electric drill; cuts what a steel pickaxe cuts.
compendium.hardwrought.info.tungsten_ste: 2400 blocks in an electric drill, faster, and through what only tungsten steel cuts.
compendium.hardwrought.info.battery_acid: Sulfur burnt and its fume taken up in the chemical reactor: oil of vitriol, for a lead-acid pack.
compendium.hardwrought.info.potash: Charcoal burnt to ash: the electrolyte of a nickel–iron cell.
compendium.hardwrought.info.sterile_dres: Cleans a wound as antiseptic does and keeps it bound twice as long as a bandage.
compendium.hardwrought.info.spoiled_food: What rotten plant food becomes. The composter takes it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.refrigerant: Ammonia driven out of bone meal in the chemical reactor, charged into steel. For compressors.
compendium.hardwrought.info.nichrome_ing: Four parts nickel to one of chromium, alloyed in the smeltery. Drawn into the wire of every heating element.
compendium.hardwrought.info.spark_plug: Fires the gasoline engine and wears out after an hour of running. Held to the engine, a new one goes in once the old is down to a quarter.
compendium.hardwrought.info.bearing: Goes into crankshafts, the gasoline engine and the Mk III machines.
compendium.hardwrought.info.diesel_gener: 64 V from diesel, kerosene or the still's fuel, joined through a copper coil. A bucket runs a 500 W load a little over twenty minutes. Its exhaust carries carbon monoxide: give it a flue.
compendium.hardwrought.info.gasoline_eng: A shaft source that runs anywhere: 48 RPM and a strength of 6144. It burns gasoline, wears spark plugs, and its exhaust is rich in carbon monoxide.
compendium.hardwrought.info.gas_burner: A clean fire for the still, the refinery and the cracker, burning natural gas or LPG. Its flame is open, so it sets firedamp off.
compendium.hardwrought.info.petroleum_la: Burns kerosene: it holds two buckets and uses 100 mB a day. An empty hand turns it on and off. It burns as long as its fuel lasts.
compendium.hardwrought.info.caustic_soda: From salt and water in the electrolyser. It etches circuit boards and goes into antiseptic.
compendium.hardwrought.info.plastic_pell: Naphtha and LPG in the chemical reactor. Pressed into sheet, and goes into resistors, transistors and oscillators.
compendium.hardwrought.info.plastic_shee: Pressed from pellets. Circuit boards, capacitors and microchips are made of it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.rubber: Resin and sulfur in the chemical reactor. It insulates wire and seals the Mk II machines.
compendium.hardwrought.info.raw_silicon: Quartz and coke in the arc furnace. The sawmill cuts it into wafers, and with steel it makes electrical steel.
compendium.hardwrought.info.silicon_wafe: Cut from raw silicon. It goes into transistors and microchips.
compendium.hardwrought.info.silicone: Silicon, naphtha and chlorine in the chemical reactor. It seals the Mk III and Mk IV machines.
compendium.hardwrought.info.circuit_boar: The base of every circuit, etched with caustic soda.
compendium.hardwrought.info.basic_circui: Goes into the Mk II machines, and is the start of every better circuit.
compendium.hardwrought.info.advanced_cir: Goes into the Mk III machines.
compendium.hardwrought.info.elite_circui: Goes into the Mk IV machines of the 240 V grid.
compendium.hardwrought.info.electrolyzer: Salt and water into caustic soda, with chlorine gas out of the top into a gas line. Runs on current.
compendium.hardwrought.info.chemical_rea: Makes plastic, rubber, silicone and the stronger medicines out of naphtha, LPG and chlorine. Runs on current.
compendium.hardwrought.info.arc_furnace: Quartz and coke into silicon, steel and silicon into electrical steel. It draws about 6 A: feed it with cable.
compendium.hardwrought.info.refractory_c: The hull of the large arc furnace: 3×3×3 of casing round a hollow hearth, with a graphite electrode in the middle of the roof.
compendium.hardwrought.info.engine_casin: The hull of the large diesel generator: 3×3×3 of casing round an engine core.
compendium.hardwrought.info.graphite_ele: Sits in the middle of the large arc furnace's roof.
compendium.hardwrought.info.engine_core: The heart of the large diesel generator, inside its hull of engine casing.
compendium.hardwrought.info.arc_furnace_: Makes silicon three times as fast as the small furnace, and steel the electric way. It draws about 13 A. An empty hand opens it, or hears what is missing.
compendium.hardwrought.info.large_diesel: Five times the current of the small generator, a fifth less fuel per joule, 16 buckets held. An empty hand opens it, or hears what is missing.
compendium.hardwrought.info.fluid_port: Takes the place of a casing block in a multiblock hull: a pipe joins it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.item_port: Takes the place of a casing block in a multiblock hull: item pipes and hoppers join it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.power_port: Takes the place of a casing block in a multiblock hull: a copper coil against it joins the machine to the line.
compendium.hardwrought.info.salt_pan: Holds four buckets of seawater and dries it to salt, two a bucket: in the sun in two minutes, over a fire in thirty seconds.
compendium.hardwrought.info.water_bowl: A bowl dipped in water takes 250 mB of it. Boiled on a campfire it comes off purified, and hot: drunk too soon, it scalds.
compendium.hardwrought.info.sand_filter: Water poured on top comes out cleaner underneath: river and swamp water become fresh. It uses up its charcoal, and salt stays in.
compendium.hardwrought.info.ceramic_filt: Turns anything but seawater into purified water, three times as fast as sand.
compendium.hardwrought.info.water_purifi: Purifies any water, seawater too, though that at a quarter of the pace. Runs on current.
compendium.hardwrought.info.dried_chamom: Oxeye daisy dried on the rack. In a bowl of water, boiled, it becomes chamomile tea for an upset stomach.
compendium.hardwrought.info.willow_bark: Comes off a birch log half the time an axe strips it. Brewed into tea it eases a fever.
compendium.hardwrought.info.chamomile_in: Boil it on a campfire into chamomile tea.
compendium.hardwrought.info.willow_infus: Boil it on a campfire into willow bark tea.
compendium.hardwrought.info.chamomile_te: Purified water, and five minutes of a settled stomach: a stomach bug is thrown off three times as fast.
compendium.hardwrought.info.willow_tea: Purified water, and five minutes of eased fever: the fever cut to 40 %%, and a cold or a wound healing twice as fast.
compendium.hardwrought.info.ashcork_log: The Ash Grove's tree, growing on netherrack in the dark. It does not burn. An axe strips two pieces of bark off each log.
compendium.hardwrought.info.ashcork_bark: Armor made of it keeps the Nether's heat off: a full set takes three quarters of the hot air's heat away.
compendium.hardwrought.info.ashcork_sapl: Grows on netherrack, in the dark.
compendium.hardwrought.info.pale_shard: Grows only in the Underworld, faintly glowing. It rekindles a dim ascent shaft, the way back up, and mends the Witch King's mantle. One is an offering of the ritual.
compendium.hardwrought.info.pale_shard_c: Pale shards grow on the walls of the Echo Chasm and, rarely, in the Stone Wastes: one of the few lights in the Underworld.
compendium.hardwrought.info.seal_stone: The Underworld seal: set below y −180 between four deepslate pillars with soul lanterns, a nether star on it opens a shaft down. It stays open for good.
compendium.hardwrought.info.ascent_shaft: The way back up out of the Underworld. Rekindled with a pale shard, its light carries whoever stands in it up beside the shaft they came down.
compendium.hardwrought.info.dragon_heart: Only a dragon raised again leaves it. Laid on the altar of a standing temple with every offering in place, it begins the ritual.
compendium.hardwrought.info.witch_king_m: Glides like elytra, and held jump drives the wearer on along their gaze at the mantle's cost. Jumping twice in the air (or X) flies as in creative, for as long as its soul charge lasts. Too high, and it gives out. Mended with pale shards.
compendium.hardwrought.info.witch_king_t: Once its king is beaten the throne goes cold, and stays a way out: sit on it for two seconds and it carries you up to its seat in the overworld. The first time, the seat is set down where you sleep.
compendium.hardwrought.info.witch_king_s: The cold throne's counterpart in the overworld. Sit on it for two seconds to be carried down to the throne. Cannot be broken; sneak and use it with empty hands to pick it up, still bound to its throne.
compendium.hardwrought.info.stale_bread: A little food from the ruins below, with a quarter chance of a stomach bug.
compendium.hardwrought.info.nether_grass: Dug by hand, like netherrack and nylium.
compendium.hardwrought.info.cast_obsidia: Water on lava sets into this, not obsidian: too brittle for a portal frame. A minute at 1600 °C in the smeltery tempers it into real obsidian. Wants a steel pickaxe.
compendium.hardwrought.info.blackstone_p: There is no stone in the Nether: blackstone breaks into pieces, and stone tools are made of these as of cobblestone pieces.
compendium.hardwrought.info.provisional_: Two running stabilisers against a frame make the portal stable: a return portal forms and everything comes through. This one runs on heat, in the Nether or wherever lava or magma touches it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.portal_stabi: Runs on current from 48 V through a copper coil, anywhere. Two against a portal's frame make it stable.
compendium.hardwrought.info.wither_essen: Falls from the Wither. The only ink soulbinding can be written in: a soulbound piece stays with its owner through one death.
compendium.hardwrought.info.bandage: Closes an open wound for five minutes, so dirt cannot get in. A new bite or heavy blow tears it off. Used like a drink.
compendium.hardwrought.info.disinfected_: Closes a wound like a bandage, and cleans some of an infection out of it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.mash: Distilled in the still with a glass bottle into spirit.
compendium.hardwrought.info.spirit: Poured on a wound it stings, closes it and cleans some infection out; the bottle comes back. It also soaks a bandage.
compendium.hardwrought.info.antiseptic: Closes a wound and cleans it far better than spirit. The bottle comes back.
compendium.hardwrought.info.fever_pills: Willow bark, only stronger: ten minutes of the fever cut to a fifth.
compendium.hardwrought.info.antibiotics: Ten minutes of antibiotics: a cold or a wound heals four times as fast, a stomach bug twice.
compendium.hardwrought.info.electrolyte_: Purified water, and five minutes of hydration coming back by itself.
compendium.hardwrought.info.gas_pump: Moves gas against the pressure, in at the back, out at the front. Standing, it is a check valve. Turned by a shaft; a hand crank will do.
compendium.hardwrought.info.electric_gas: Pumps four times as fast as a gas pump, on current through a coil.
compendium.hardwrought.info.transformer: Steps 60 V up to 240 V and, fed from its bushing, down again. The same power on a quarter of the current loses a sixteenth on the line. Above 4 A out of its high side it chars; a new winding mends it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.porcelain_in: Stands 1000 V in the rain, where glazed brick flashes over above 150 V.
compendium.hardwrought.info.bushing: A coil in a porcelain sleeve: where a line at high voltage goes into a transformer.
compendium.hardwrought.info.high_voltage: A line mast with a porcelain insulator, for 240 V. Bare wire at 240 V kills within seconds: keep it high.
compendium.hardwrought.info.knife_switch: Joins the coils set against it while closed: thrown by hand, or following a redstone signal. It is set down open.
compendium.hardwrought.info.fuse_box: Blows after half a second at 6 A, before the wire behind it burns through. A new fuse cartridge mends it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.breaker: Trips at 16 A and is closed again by hand.
compendium.hardwrought.info.coil_winder: Winds eight lengths of enamelled wire into one winding. Runs on current.
compendium.hardwrought.info.insulated_wi: Bites nobody, goes through walls and does not leak in the rain, but spans only 12 blocks.
compendium.hardwrought.info.electrical_s: Steel and raw silicon in the arc furnace, pressed into plates for transformer cores and the Mk IV machines.
compendium.hardwrought.info.enamelled_wi: Copper wire in resin varnish: the coil winder winds eight into a winding.
compendium.hardwrought.info.winding: Goes into transformers and the Mk IV machines, and mends a burnt-out transformer.
compendium.hardwrought.info.porcelain: Fired from a porcelain blank. It stands high voltage in the rain, and fuses are made of it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.fuse_cartrid: Goes into a fuse box, and replaces one that blew.
compendium.minecraft.info.torch: A burning torch. It burns for a day wherever it is, in the hand, the bag or on a wall, and then it is a stick. A torch taken down comes off burning, with what it had left. Held to a laid campfire it lights it; in hand it sets off firedamp.
compendium.hardwrought.info.unlit_torch: Torches come out of the grid unlit. Set one down and light it where it stands, or hold one to a fire, lava, a lit furnace or a burning light, or light it in hand with flint and steel, the lighting sticks or a burning torch in the other hand.
compendium.minecraft.info.lantern: Burns for three days, then goes dark; flint and steel lights it again.
compendium.minecraft.info.campfire: A fire pit, set down laid, not lit: lighting sticks, flint and steel or a burning torch start it. It burns two days, boils water, bakes clay and casts the soft metals. Indoors it eats the air.
compendium.minecraft.info.crafting_table: The first bench is not crafted but hewn out of a standing log with an iron axe. The crafting table is joinery, six boards three wide, and takes a bench to make.
compendium.minecraft.info.furnace: Furnaces bring raw ore and metal to working heat rather than smelting it, and the bar is beaten out on the anvil. Powder is cast straight into ingots. Nothing above 1550 °C melts in one.
compendium.minecraft.info.gravel: Breaks into flint shards and loose stones. River gravel also gives tin ore, one grain in twenty.
compendium.minecraft.info.clay_ball: Baked on a campfire into brick. Four bricks make the first furnace.
compendium.minecraft.info.brick: Four in the inventory square make a brick furnace.
compendium.minecraft.info.oxeye_daisy: Dried on a drying rack into chamomile.
compendium.minecraft.info.birch_log: Stripped with an axe, it gives willow bark half the time.
compendium.minecraft.info.golden_apple: Not food: it fills nothing and is eaten for what it does, stamina regeneration on top of the rest.
compendium.minecraft.info.enchanted_gold: Made again from eight blocks of gold. Stamina regeneration III on top of the rest.
compendium.minecraft.info.water_bucket: Water is finite: a bucket takes exactly one block and leaves the rest. It remembers what is in it, salt, swamp, river, fresh or purified, and pours it back out.
compendium.minecraft.info.glass_bottle: Takes a tenth of a block of water, and keeps its kind.
compendium.minecraft.info.bowl: Dipped in water it takes 250 mB; boiled on a campfire it is purified.
compendium.minecraft.info.shield: Raised just in time, it parries: most of the hit is stopped and the attacker staggers. Later it only blocks, for stamina. An axe's heavy blow breaks the guard.
compendium.minecraft.info.nether_star: Falls where the Wither dies. Set into the seal stone deep under the overworld, it opens the way into the Underworld. One is an offering of the ritual.
compendium.minecraft.info.wither_skeleto: Empty until it has lain half a minute in soul fire. Only three soul-charged skulls raise the Wither.
compendium.minecraft.info.echo_shard: From the ancient cities of the deep dark. Four go into the seal stone that opens the Underworld.
compendium.minecraft.info.grindstone: Finishes a forged or cast part: hold it in hand, use the stone and keep the marker in the band for eight passes. It also takes rust off steel.
compendium.minecraft.info.smithing_table: Works a piece up a tier, tungsten steel to netherite, then mithril, then adamant, by tracing the template's pattern. The trace decides the craftsmanship.
compendium.minecraft.info.enchanting_tab: Runes are written onto the piece in lapis powder, laid by hand on its outline: the more of a rune lies on it, the higher the level. Bookshelves and levels decide which runes lie ready.
compendium.minecraft.info.anvil: The smith's anvil: hammer in the main hand, hot metal in the off hand. Better than wood, up to 100 %% craftsmanship.
compendium.minecraft.info.flint_and_stee: Lights campfires, burnt-out torches and dark lanterns. It wears with use.
compendium.minecraft.info.obsidian: Takes a steel pickaxe. Water on lava gives only brittle cast obsidian.
compendium.minecraft.info.cauldron: Remembers what water was poured into it, and gives the same back.
compendium.minecraft.info.netherite_ingo: Works tungsten steel up to netherite at a smithing table. Diamond gear cannot be made at all.
compendium.minecraft.info.diamond: Diamond tools and armor cannot be made, and steel takes their place where they turn up. The diamond itself stays.
compendium.minecraft.info.leather: Pads forged armor: a helmet shell takes one, sabatons one, greaves two, a cuirass three.

message.hardwrought.party.result.not_lea: Only the party leader can do that.
