message.hardwrought.party.result.not_mem: Nobody by that name is in your party.
message.hardwrought.encounter.burden_you: Soul burden on you! Gather the others – together you carry it.
message.hardwrought.encounter.burden: Soul burden on %s! Stand with them to share it.
message.hardwrought.encounter.brand_you: You are branded! Get away from the others!
message.hardwrought.encounter.tether: Void tether with %s! Pull apart until it snaps.
message.hardwrought.encounter.crystal_ch: The next crystal must fall within %s seconds!
message.hardwrought.encounter.crystal_re: Too slow – a soul crystal rises again.
death.attack.hardwrought.radiation.playe: %1$s died of radiation sickness while fighting %2$s
multiblock.hardwrought.reactor.note: Ports may take the place of any wall block but the middle of the head. Each place of the head's middle takes a rod drive or wall; four drives at least to shut down a fresh core.
multiblock.hardwrought.steam_turbine.not: Steam in through a gas port, current out through a power port with a copper coil on it, water out through a fluid port.
multiblock.hardwrought.centrifuge_cascad: Feed in through a gas port in a wall or the floor, product out through a gas port in the roof, depleted uranium out through an item port.
recipe.hardwrought.reactor.instruction: In a running reactor: fuel in a channel, purified feedwater by pipe, steam out by gas line.
recipe.hardwrought.meltdown.instruction: What is left when a reactor core melts.
recipe.hardwrought.centrifuge_cascade.in: In a centrifuge cascade (a multiblock) on current: hexafluoride in by gas line through a wall, enriched out through the roof.
message.hardwrought.reactor.meltdown: A reactor core has melted. Keep away from the debris.
gui.hardwrought.turbine.how: Steam by gas line into a gas port; a copper coil on the power port.
journal.hardwrought.rock_that_ticks.text: The heavy green-black ore deep in the granite is uranium. It is barely dangerous to hold, but it is never quite still. A glass tube of thin gas round a fine wire clicks every time something passes through it: a Geiger counter. Held in the hand, it tells me how much is about.
journal.hardwrought.yellowcake.title: Yellowcake
journal.hardwrought.yellowcake.text: Uranium powder, leached with oil of vitriol in the chemical reactor, gives a yellow oxide. That is what a uranium mine sells.
journal.hardwrought.the_fluorine.title: The fluorine
journal.hardwrought.the_fluorine.text: The purple stone that grows beside the uranium is fluorite. With oil of vitriol it gives off a fume that eats glass: hydrofluoric acid. With it, yellowcake becomes uranium hexafluoride, a gas.
journal.hardwrought.spinning_it_apart.te: Only seven parts in a thousand of uranium burn in a reactor. As a gas, spun faster than sound, the heavy part is flung outwards and the light part stays by the axis. Five centrifuges in a hall: ten parts of gas in, one part enriched out, and the rest is depleted uranium.
journal.hardwrought.zirconium.title: Zirconium
journal.hardwrought.zirconium.text: Thorium powder cracked with caustic soda leaves zircon behind. Chlorinated over coke it gives zirconium sponge, and a little hafnium. The sponge, remelted with tin under the large arc, is zircaloy: it lets neutrons through and does not rust in hot water.
journal.hardwrought.the_fuel.title: The fuel
journal.hardwrought.the_fuel.text: Enriched gas with water becomes black uranium dioxide; pressed and fired, pellets. Four pellets in a zircaloy tube, a spring and two plugs make a fuel rod; six rods, a spacer grid and two nozzles a fuel assembly.
journal.hardwrought.the_pile.title: The pile
journal.hardwrought.the_pile.text: A vessel of five by five by five: graphite above and below, nine fuel channels between, rod drives on the head. Eight fresh assemblies go critical, nine have reserve. The rods hang on magnets: without current they fall in.
journal.hardwrought.steam_and_current.te: The core boils purified water to steam. A turbine takes it by gas line, gives 240 volts, and sends the condensed water back.
journal.hardwrought.fertile_thorium.text: Thorium does not burn, but in a running core it takes neutrons and becomes uranium-233. A breeder rod in a channel, reprocessed afterwards, gives fuel without centrifuges, and it shines fiercely.
journal.hardwrought.lore.the_atom_fuel_c:
• Raw uranium → crusher → uranium powder
• 4 uranium powder + battery acid → chemical reactor → 2 yellowcake
• 2 fluorite + battery acid → chemical reactor → hydrofluoric acid
• yellowcake + 2 hydrofluoric acid → chemical reactor → 10 units of UF₆ gas (out at the top)
• 10 UF₆ → centrifuge cascade → 1 enriched UF₆ + depleted uranium
• 1 enriched UF₆ + 250 mB water → chemical reactor → 2 uranium dioxide
• uranium dioxide → plate press → 4 green pellets → glass kiln → fuel pellets
• zircaloy plate → tube mill → 2 cladding tubes

Thorium: 2 thorium powder + caustic soda → thorium dioxide and zircon. 4 zircon + coke + chlorine → zirconium sponge and hafnium. 4 sponge + tin in the large arc furnace → 4 zircaloy.
journal.hardwrought.lore.the_atom_runnin:
The core follows real point kinetics. Reactivity ρ is shown in units and in dollars; one dollar is prompt critical, and then the power runs away in a fraction of a second. Draw the rods slowly: below a tenth of a dollar the power doubles in about a minute.

The power port feeds the coolant pumps and the rod drives (at least 30 V, full flow at 60 V). Without current the rods drop. Without pumps only natural circulation is left: enough for decay heat, not for power. Feedwater must be purified; the steam drum stands at up to 30 bar, so steam lines must be chromium or titanium.

At full power a fresh core makes 120 kW of heat and lasts two hours. The turbine turns a third of it into current. After a shutdown, xenon builds up for a while: a hot reactor may not restart at once. A redstone signal on the desk scrams the core.
journal.hardwrought.lore.the_atom_radiat:
Dose is counted in sieverts and adds up on the body; the body mends it, halving it over about forty minutes. From half a sievert nausea, from one radiation sickness, from three it costs health, from six it kills.

Natural uranium is nearly harmless to carry. A fresh fuel assembly gives half a millisievert an hour. A spent one gives twelve sieverts an hour: carried, it kills in half an hour. A running core gives a thousand sieverts an hour at a metre. Between it and you, every block counts: lead lets a fiftieth through, the vessel wall a twentieth, concrete less than a sixth, rock a quarter, water a third.
journal.hardwrought.lore.the_atom_when_i:
The protection drops the rods by itself above 350 °C, above 115 % power, when the pumps stop at power, when the feedwater runs out, or when the drives lose current. Then only decay heat is left: a few percent at once, one percent after an hour.

A core that has run long and loses all its water still heats on decay heat. At 1200 °C the cladding bursts and throws radioactive debris about. At 2200 °C the core melts: the vessel blows open, the fuel becomes corium, and debris is scattered far around. Keep the feedwater coming, and never leave fewer than four rod drives on the head.
compendium.hardwrought.info.fluorite_ore: Purple and green crystals in granite, often near uranium. Any stone pickaxe breaks it; it gives fluorite.
compendium.hardwrought.info.reactor_vess: Steel plate over concrete and lead: the 5×5×5 reactor's walls, and a shield that lets a twentieth of its radiation through.
compendium.hardwrought.info.fuel_channel: The nine blocks of the reactor's core layer. Each takes one fuel assembly or one thorium breeder rod.
compendium.hardwrought.info.control_rod_: Stands in the middle of the reactor's head. Each is worth 5 % reactivity fully in. Without current its rod drops.
compendium.hardwrought.info.reactor_cont: The reactor's control desk, in the middle of one side of the vessel. Fuel, rods, scram and every reading.
compendium.hardwrought.info.turbine_casi: The casing of the steam turbine, a 3×3×3 multiblock.
compendium.hardwrought.info.turbine_roto: The turbine's centre: rows of blades on a shaft.
compendium.hardwrought.info.condenser: Under the turbine's rotor: the spent steam becomes purified water again, 95 % of it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.turbine_cont: The steam turbine's controller. 240 V through a power port, as stiff as a large diesel; a third of the steam's heat becomes current.
compendium.hardwrought.info.centrifuge_c: The clean hall of the centrifuge cascade, a 3×3×3 multiblock.
compendium.hardwrought.info.gas_centrifu: Five stand in the cascade's middle layer: the centre and the four corners.
compendium.hardwrought.info.centrifuge_c: The cascade's controller. Ten units of natural UF₆ give one of enriched, and depleted uranium.
compendium.hardwrought.info.corium: A melted core, set: 200 Sv/h at a metre. Burns what stands on it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.radioactive_: Thrown out of a burst core: 50 mSv/h at a metre.
compendium.hardwrought.info.gas_port: A port of any big machine for a gas line: steam out of a reactor and into a turbine, uranium hexafluoride through the cascade.
compendium.hardwrought.info.fluorite: Calcium fluoride. With battery acid in the chemical reactor: hydrofluoric acid.
compendium.hardwrought.info.hydrofluoric: Turns yellowcake into uranium hexafluoride, and dissolves bred thorium.
compendium.hardwrought.info.yellowcake: Uranium oxide leached out of the ore with battery acid.
compendium.hardwrought.info.uranium_diox: Enriched uranium as a ceramic powder. The plate press makes green pellets of it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.green_pellet: Pressed but unfired: the glass kiln sinters it into a fuel pellet.
compendium.hardwrought.info.fuel_pellet: Four go into each fuel rod.
compendium.hardwrought.info.depleted_ura: The tails of enrichment. Dense; a block of uranium shields like lead.
compendium.hardwrought.info.thorium_diox: Pressed into thorium pellets for breeder rods.
compendium.hardwrought.info.thorium_pell: Four go into each thorium breeder rod.
compendium.hardwrought.info.zircon: Left over when monazite is cracked. Chlorinated over coke: zirconium and hafnium.
compendium.hardwrought.info.zirconium_sp: Four, with a tin ingot, in the large arc furnace: four zircaloy ingots.
compendium.hardwrought.info.hafnium: Swallows neutrons: three make a control rod.
compendium.hardwrought.info.cladding_tub: Zircaloy plate drawn into tube on the tube mill.
compendium.hardwrought.info.plenum_sprin: Holds the pellet stack of a rod together.
compendium.hardwrought.info.spacer_grid: Holds the rods of an assembly apart.
compendium.hardwrought.info.top_nozzle: The head of a fuel assembly.
compendium.hardwrought.info.bottom_nozzl: The foot of a fuel assembly, with a debris filter.
compendium.hardwrought.info.thorium_bree: In a fuel channel of a running reactor it breeds uranium-233. It costs reactivity while it does.
compendium.hardwrought.info.irradiated_t: 5 Sv/h. With hydrofluoric acid in the chemical reactor: enriched hexafluoride. Move it by pipe, not by hand.
compendium.hardwrought.info.control_rod: Hafnium, or silver, in stainless steel. Goes into a control rod drive.
compendium.hardwrought.info.turbine_blad: Eight go into a turbine rotor.
compendium.hardwrought.info.impeller: The main coolant pump's wheel, built into the reactor's desk.
compendium.hardwrought.info.fission_cham: A neutron detector; two in the reactor's desk.
compendium.hardwrought.info.geiger_muell: The heart of a Geiger counter.
compendium.hardwrought.info.centrifuge_r: The spinning heart of a gas centrifuge.
compendium.hardwrought.info.fuel_assembl: Goes into a fuel channel while the core is shut down. Lasts two hours at full power; 0.5 mSv/h fresh.
compendium.hardwrought.info.spent_fuel_a: 12 Sv/h: deadly within half an hour. Keep it under water or behind lead, and move it by pipe.
compendium.hardwrought.info.geiger_count: Held in either hand it clicks and reads the dose rate; used, it reads the dose taken.
compendium.hardwrought.info.zircaloy_ing: Zirconium with a little tin, from the large arc furnace. Hardly takes up neutrons.
gui.hardwrought.reactor.setpoint_down.ti: Automatic control: lower the target power by 10 %. Below 10 % the rods go back to hand control.
gui.hardwrought.reactor.setpoint_up.tip: Automatic control: raise the target power by 10 %. The desk then draws the rods out by itself, slowly and safely, and holds that power. The easy way to run a reactor.
gui.hardwrought.reactor.reset.tip: After an emergency shutdown: clears it once its cause is gone, so the reactor can be started again.
gui.hardwrought.reactor.scram.tip: Emergency shutdown: all rods drop into the core at once and the chain reaction stops.
gui.hardwrought.reactor.insert_more.tip: By hand: drive the rods 10 % further in (less power).
gui.hardwrought.reactor.insert.tip: By hand: drive the rods 1 % further in (less power).
gui.hardwrought.reactor.withdraw.tip: By hand: draw the rods 1 % out (more power). Careful: a few percent too far and the power runs away; the protection then shuts the reactor down.
gui.hardwrought.reactor.withdraw_more.ti: By hand: draw the rods 10 % out (more power). Dangerous: better use Auto +.
gui.hardwrought.reactor.rods_bar.tip: Control rods: %s%% in the core (dark), going to %s%% (orange mark). In = no chain reaction, out = power.
gui.hardwrought.reactor.hint.tripped: Emergency shutdown: %s. Fix that, then press Reset.
gui.hardwrought.reactor.hint.power: No current: put a copper coil on the power port and wire it to 60 V (a diesel generator will do).
gui.hardwrought.reactor.hint.drives: Only %s control rod drives in the lid: at least 4 are needed to shut the reactor down.
gui.hardwrought.reactor.hint.water: No feedwater: pipe purified water into the fluid port (water treatment first).
gui.hardwrought.reactor.hint.fuel: %s of 9 fuel assemblies: put at least 8 into the slots on the left.
gui.hardwrought.reactor.hint.ready: Ready. Press Auto + to start up; the desk does the rest.
gui.hardwrought.reactor.hint.venting: Steam is blown off: lead it through the gas port to a steam turbine (chromium or titanium gas line).
gui.hardwrought.reactor.hint.starting: Starting up: the rods come out slowly until the core goes critical. It takes a few minutes.
gui.hardwrought.reactor.hint.running: Running. The steam goes through the gas port to the turbine.
gui.hardwrought.reactor.hint.climbing: Starting up: the chain reaction is growing, the power ×10 every %s s. It shows once it passes 0.1 %%.
multiblock.hardwrought.battery_bank.note: Up to 27 cell stacks inside; fewer work too, with less capacity. A copper coil on the power port.
compendium.hardwrought.info.heavy_power_: Insulated, 0.002 Ω per block, 80 A, spans 16. Wire a turbine to its transformer with it.
compendium.hardwrought.info.overhead_con: Bare aluminium on a steel core: 0.006 Ω per block, 40 A, spans 48 between masts. Meant for high voltage, on porcelain.
compendium.hardwrought.info.power_transf: Steps up or down four times like the small one, but carries 60 A on its high side through 0.05 Ω. A turbine's 240 V become 960 V for a long line.
compendium.hardwrought.info.battery_bank: The hull of the battery bank, a 5×5×5 multiblock.
compendium.hardwrought.info.battery_cell: Inside the battery bank: each holds 2 MJ and carries 10 A. 27 of them hold 15 kWh.
compendium.hardwrought.info.battery_bank: The battery bank on the 240-volt line: 216 V empty to 252 V full. It charges from above that and gives below it. Too much current boils the acid.
gui.hardwrought.battery_bank.no_stacks: No cell stacks inside: fill the 3×3×3 inside with battery cell stacks.
gui.hardwrought.battery_bank.no_line: No line: put a copper coil on the power port and string heavy cable from it to a source.
gui.hardwrought.battery_bank.too_low: The line stands at %s V, not above the bank's %s V, so it cannot charge. It needs more: a turbine at 240 V, or 60 V stepped up four times by a transformer.
compendium.hardwrought.info.high_power_c: Copper in oil-filled paper under a lead sheath: 0.0008 Ω per block, 300 A, insulated, spans 24. What many turbines feed their transformers through.
compendium.hardwrought.info.firebox: Burns coal, charcoal, coke or logs under a boiler: 10 kW. Lit with a flint and steel; hoppers feed it. A redstone signal closes its damper, down to a fifth of heat and fuel.
compendium.hardwrought.info.boiler: Water in by pipe or bucket, steam out by gas line. Rated for 10 bar, bursts above 16. Any water but purified leaves scale; running dry ruins it. An empty hand reads it, a pickaxe descales it cold, an iron plate patches a leak.
compendium.hardwrought.info.safety_valve: Sits on top of a boiler and blows off steam above its setting, 4 to 12 bar. An empty hand turns the spring. Without one a boiler holds whatever its fire makes, until it bursts.
compendium.hardwrought.info.steam_engine: A shaft source at 32 RPM, fed steam by gas line. From 1.5 bar it turns over, from 8 bar it gives its full 3072. A governor lets in only what the load needs; redstone shuts its throttle.
compendium.hardwrought.info.steam_whistl: Sounds when pulled by hand or by redstone, if there is at least 1 bar of steam behind it. Higher pressure, higher note.
compendium.hardwrought.info.gas_valve: A stop valve in iron gas line. Shut by its hand wheel or by a redstone signal, it parts the line in two.
compendium.hardwrought.info.steam_cylind: Cylinder, piston, rod and slide valve: the heart of a steam engine.
message.hardwrought.boiler.too_hot: Too hot to work on: let it cool and its pressure down first
message.hardwrought.boiler.descaled: The scale comes off the tubes
message.hardwrought.boiler.patched: A patch riveted over the worst seam
message.hardwrought.steam_engine.reading: %s bar at the inlet · %s RPM · load %s%%
death.attack.hardwrought.scalding.player: %1$s was scalded by live steam while fighting %2$s
journal.hardwrought.raising_steam.title: Raising steam
journal.hardwrought.raising_steam.text: A firebox of brick and iron, a drum of riveted plate on it, water in the drum. Fire under water makes steam, and steam shut in makes pressure.
journal.hardwrought.the_safety_valve.tex: A drum that only fills will one day burst. A spring-loaded valve on top lets off what is too much, before the iron does.
journal.hardwrought.steam_at_work.title: Steam at work
journal.hardwrought.steam_at_work.text: Steam pushes a piston, the piston a crank, the crank a shaft. More than any wheel in a river ever gave, and anywhere I can bring fuel and water.
A wheel on the line to shut it, a whistle to be heard across the valley. Steam is mine to send where I want it.
journal.hardwrought.lore.steam_raising_s:
The boiler stands on its firebox. The firebox burns coal, charcoal, coke or logs and gives 10 kW; it must be lit with a flint and steel, and hoppers can feed it. A redstone signal closes the damper: the fire smoulders at a fifth of its heat and its fuel. A gas burner gives 8 kW, a forge 5 kW, a furnace 3 kW, a campfire 1.5 kW.

The boiler holds 4 buckets of water, by pipe or bucket. First the fire heats the iron and the water, about a minute and a half on a full firebox. At 100 °C the water boils; but the steam stays in the drum, the pressure climbs, and with it the boiling point: about 180 °C at 10 bar. Every 4 kJ of heat past that make one unit of steam out of 2 mB of water. A full fire makes about 2 units a second.

A hot boiler is a store of heat: when an engine draws steam and the pressure falls, the hot water flashes to fresh steam. So it rides out a sudden load, and takes minutes to come up from cold. An empty hand reads its temperature, pressure, water, scale and damage. Steam leaves by gas line: iron line holds 12 bar, bronze only 6.
journal.hardwrought.lore.steam_engines_a:
The steam engine takes steam by gas line on any side but its back, where its axle leaves into a shaft. It turns at 32 RPM. Its strength follows the pressure at its inlet: it turns over from 1.5 bar and gives its full 3072 from 8 bar.

A governor lets in only what the line asks: 0.2 units a second running light, up to 3.2 under full load. A full firebox therefore keeps about two thirds of an engine at full strength; two boilers on one line keep a whole one. A redstone signal shuts its throttle.

The safety valve sits on top of the boiler and lifts above its setting, 4, 6, 8, 10 or 12 bar; an empty hand turns its spring. Set it under what the weakest line holds.

The stop valve is a piece of iron line with a hand wheel: shut, it parts the line in two. A redstone signal shuts it too. The steam whistle sounds when pulled or powered, as long as there is 1 bar behind it.
journal.hardwrought.lore.steam_when_it_g:
Pressure. A sound boiler bursts above 16 bar, and the iron strains already above 85 % of that. Without a safety valve nothing stops the pressure; the explosion tears the boiler apart and scalds everyone near.

Running dry. Without water the fire heats bare iron. Above 300 °C it is ruined, quickly. Water fed into iron above 350 °C flashes to steam at once and bursts the boiler. Never refill a boiler that has run dry while it is still hot.

Scale. Every water but purified leaves scale on the tubes: fresh water a little, river water more, swamp water much, seawater a great deal. Scale keeps the heat from the water, up to half of it, and once the tubes are more than half furred up the iron under it overheats. A pickaxe chips it off a boiler under 50 °C.

Leaks. From a quarter damage the boiler leaks steam at its seams, and the steam scalds whoever stands beside it. The more damaged, the lower it bursts: at full damage already at 8 bar. An iron plate rivets a patch over the worst seam and takes off a quarter of the damage, on a boiler under 100 °C and without pressure.

Lines. A gas line bursts at its weakest pipe when a store on it stands above that pipe's limit. A burst steam line scalds everyone close by.
